text:
alex: FYI — proposing we change default SIEM export retention for dev/test tenants from 180d -> 90d to cut storage costs. Need eng-security + legal signoff because of KMS and compliance implications.

maya: Can we do tiered retention instead? e.g. 30d raw, 90d redacted, 365d aggregated summary. That would keep short-term forensic ability without hoarding raw events.

jon-p: Main concern: some vuln/IR digests still require access >90d. How do we give analysts time-limited access for investigations without widening RBAC?

lia: @alex who owns the CMK used for exports? If retention changes, do key policies need updates? Also we must retain KMS key usage logs for any policy/grant changes.

alex: CMK is `service/export-cmk`. Current key policy allows `security-admins` decrypt. Proposal keeps that but adds an "export_unseal" workflow that mints ephemeral grants.

secops-bot: INCIDENT-1234: snapshot export created by jon-p at 1779991000. Reminder: follow export checklist https://redwood/internal/export-playbook :white_check_mark: 

maya: I want to avoid the old mass-unmasking pattern. Suggest: timeboxed signed requests with ticket ID in metadata + 2 approvers for exports longer than 30d.

jon-p: Draft ticket template (I'll iterate):
```
Request: SIEM export unseal
Requester: <name>
Reason: vuln triage / IR
Scope: tenant X, date range
Retention requested: <days>
Approvers: @approver1 @approver2
Ticket ID: <TICKET-#>
```

lia: For RBAC: propose new role `siem_export_analyst` with read-only SIEM view + permission to request ephemeral unseal. Role should be constrained by org/tenant and require enforced MFA.

alex: Agree on role. Also want to automate KMS ephemeral grants that expire (TTL). Does AWS grants / CMK support TTL-style grants for our use? If so we can auto-revoke.

maya: AWS supports grants + envelope keys; ephemeral grants are doable. We must be careful with key rotation so exported artifacts remain decryptable. Keep an encrypted copy in S3 with rotation-aware envelope keys.

security-ops: Legal flagged certain event classes that require 365d retention. We need a mapping: event_type -> retention + redaction rules. Who owns this mapping?

alex: I'll own the mapping doc and add columns: event_class, default_retention, redaction_required, legal_notes, exception_process.

jon-p: I'll open a short RFC with the proposed roles, grant flow, and infra diagram. Can we do a 30m sync with legal + infra next week?

maya: Next Wed 10am PT works for me.

alex: I'll send invite and open a PR in infra for the grant automation POC (grant TTL = 7d to start).

lia: One more ask: audit trail for who requested/approved exports must be pushed into WORM storage for 1yr. Add this to the playbook.

alex: Noted — will update the playbook with the WORM requirement and attach sample S3 lifecycle policy.

secops-bot: Reminder: include `ticket:` prefix in S3 object metadata for traceability.

jon-p: Uploaded draft ticket template to https://docs.redwood/siem/export-request-template.md — feedback welcome.

maya: Quick Q: redaction — pipeline or analyst-side? I prefer pre-export (pipeline) with QA checks.

lia: Pre-export pipeline + a QA validation step. Add a unit eval that checks for PII classes before export.

alex: OK. Targeting rollout next sprint. If any blockers, tag me directly.

maya: Thanks all. I'll add review comments on the RFC tonight. :thumbsup:
